parts.goal: Write your first real Python programs. Study each lesson in order. Practice after every lesson.

sections.title: What Is Python
sections.body:
Python is a high-level programming language.

Why it is popular:
- Easy to read
- Powerful
- Used in AI, web, automation, data science

Exercise:
List 5 products that use Python.

sections.title: Installation
sections.body:
Install:
1. Python
2. VS Code
3. Python extension

Verify:
python --version

Exercise:

sections.body:
Your first program:

print("Hello, World!")

Change the message three times.

sections.body:

name="Ali"
age=18
height=1.75

sections.body:

int
float
bool

sections.body:
name=input("Your name: ")

sections.body:

+ - * / // % **

== != < > <= >=

Logical:
and or not

parts.goal: Learn how programs make decisions and repeat work.

sections.title: Conditions
sections.body:
Conditions let a program choose what to do.

Example:
if score >= 50:
    print("Passed")
else:
    print("Failed")

Practice:
Create a program that checks if a person is an adult.

sections.title: Comparison Operators
sections.body:
Operators:
==
!=
<
>
<=
>=

Exercise:
Predict the result of 20 comparisons before running them.

sections.title: Logical Operators
sections.body:
Logical operators:
and
or
not

Example:
age >= 18 and has_id == True

Practice:
Write 10 logical expressions.

sections.title: If Elif Else
sections.body:
Use elif when there are multiple choices.

Example:
90-100 -> A
80-89 -> B
70-79 -> C

Project:
Grade Calculator.

sections.title: For Loops
sections.body:
A for loop repeats a fixed number of times.

Example:
for i in range(1,11):
    print(i)

Practice:
Print numbers 1-100.
Print even numbers.
Print odd numbers.

sections.title: While Loops
sections.body:
A while loop repeats while a condition is true.

Example:
count = 1
while count <= 5:
    print(count)
    count += 1

Practice:
Countdown from 10 to 1.

sections.title: Nested Loops
sections.body:
Loops can contain other loops.

Example:
Print a multiplication table.

Challenge:
Print star patterns:
*
**
***
****
*****

sections.body:
Common mistakes:
- Infinite loops
- Wrong indentation
- Incorrect conditions
- Off-by-one errors

Find and fix five buggy examples.

parts.goal: Learn to break programs into reusable, organized functions.

sections.title: Why Functions
sections.body:
Functions let you reuse code instead of repeating it.

Benefits:
- Cleaner code
- Easier testing
- Easier maintenance

Exercise:
List five repeated tasks that could become functions.

sections.title: Defining Functions
sections.body:
Example:

def greet():
    print("Hello!")

greet()

Practice:
Create functions that print your name, city and favorite subject.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.body:
Parameters let functions receive information.

Example:

def greet(name):
    print("Hello", name)

Practice:
Create functions with 1, 2 and 3 parameters.

sections.title: Return
sections.body:
Return sends a value back.

Example:

def add(a,b):
    return a+b

Practice:
Create functions for subtraction, multiplication and division.

sections.title: Scope
sections.body:
Variables may be local or global.

Understand where variables can be accessed.

Exercise:
Predict which variables exist inside and outside functions.

sections.title: Lambda
sections.body:
Lambda creates small anonymous functions.

Example:
square = lambda x: x*x

Practice:
Create lambda functions for cube, even check and uppercase text.

sections.title: Recursion
sections.body:
A recursive function calls itself.

Always include a base case.

Practice:
Describe how to calculate factorial recursively before writing code.

sections.body:

- Missing return
- Wrong parameter count
- Infinite recursion
- Name errors

sections.body: Embeddings convert text into vectors that capture semantic meaning. Explore similarity search and cosine similarity concepts.

sections.title: Fine Tuning
sections.body: Compare prompt engineering, RAG and fine-tuning. Learn supervised fine-tuning workflow and common use cases.

sections.title: LoRA QLoRA
sections.body: Study parameter-efficient fine-tuning with LoRA and QLoRA. Understand why they reduce hardware requirements.

sections.title: RLHF
sections.body: Learn the idea behind Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and why preference data improves model behavior.

sections.title: Model Optimization
sections.body: Topics: quantization, batching, KV cache, model serving, GPU memory optimization and inference speed.

sections.title: vLLM and Deployment
sections.body: Understand production inference with vLLM, load balancing, autoscaling, monitoring and rolling updates.

sections.title: Benchmarking
sections.body: Measure latency, throughput, accuracy, cost and reliability. Learn why benchmarks should match real workloads.

sections.title: Debugging
sections.body: Investigate hallucinations, context overflow, prompt failures, retrieval failures and deployment issues.

sections.title: Big Project
sections.body: Big Project: Design an enterprise-grade LLM platform including API gateway, model serving, RAG, vector database, monitoring, evaluation and security.

sections.title: Interview
sections.body: Interview: Transformer vs RNN? What is attention? Why embeddings? RAG vs Fine-tuning? Why LoRA? Why quantization?

sections.title: CheatSheet
sections.body: Cheat Sheet: Transformer, Attention, Tokens, Embeddings, LoRA, RLHF, Quantization, vLLM, RAG, Benchmarking.

sections.title: Final Exam
sections.body: Final Exam: Design a complete production LLM architecture serving millions of users while balancing latency, cost, safety and reliability.
